definitions.explanation: To significantly modify or rebuild a building's structure, often involving major changes to the layout or basic framework.

examples.japanese: {古民家|こみんか}を{改築|かいちく}してカフェにした。
examples.english: We renovated an old traditional house and turned it into a café.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{改築|かいちく}{工事|こうじ}が{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: The station renovation work is progressing.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}を{改築|かいちく}するか{建|た}て{替|か}えるか{迷|まよ}っている。
examples.english: I'm deciding whether to renovate or completely rebuild the house.

notes:
USAGE: {改築|かいちく} refers to significant structural changes to a building. It differs from {改装|かいそう} (interior renovation) and {修繕|しゅうぜん} (repairs).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{改築|かいちく}{工事|こうじ} (renovation work)
・{改築|かいちく}{費用|ひよう} (renovation costs)
・{家|いえ}を{改築|かいちく}する (to renovate a house)

DISTINCTION FROM SIMILAR TERMS:
・{新築|しんちく} - new construction (building from scratch)
・{改築|かいちく} - renovation with major structural changes
・{改装|かいそう} - interior renovation, remodeling
・{増築|ぞうちく} - building an addition/extension
・{修繕|しゅうぜん} - repairs, fixing damage
・{建|た}て{替|か}え - complete rebuild (tear down and build new)
